findings.claim: The supplied router and capability manifest agree on six admitted foundation procedures: queries identity.session, identity.scopes, identity.entry and identity.syncCredentials; commands identity.createInitialBond and authority.refreshSnapshot. All are declared app-only with session assurance and requiredEvidence G2.

The router requires identity and platform context. syncCredentials explicitly reports SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE without an issuer. These source guards do not prove deployed authentication or authorization coverage.

The catalog's literal empty-v1-contract description is inconsistent with the six current handlers. Its narrower empty-business-contract/router language remains consistent with a foundation-only API; it must not erase current foundation admission or imply business implementation authority.

The governing policy still authorizes horizontal foundation work and explicitly defers business admission. Its description of two read-only identity procedures needs reconciliation with the six foundation procedures, including two commands. This descriptive drift does not itself revoke the governing scope restriction.

Business procedures are not authorized by these sources. Feature migrations and unresolved product-policy decisions require subsequent admission; historical evidence and architecture gate success cannot substitute for current feature or authorization evidence.
The manifest declares G2 as required evidence while its comment still asks the owner to confirm that admission bar. Neither actual G2 results nor deployed runtime evidence is included.
